subject.title: fix(update): dev channel update builds from an unverified checkout at the git install path

question: Should package-to-dev conversion intentionally reject every existing OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR, including empty and canonical OpenClaw checkouts, to guarantee a freshly created trust boundary?
rationale: The safer behavior deliberately breaks a previously documented and accepted conversion path, so automation should not make the compatibility-versus-trust decision on the repository's behalf.

options.title: Adopt fresh-only conversion
options.body: Confirm the breaking policy, replace retry sidecars with atomic SQLite state, and land with fresh-install and interrupted-upgrade proof.

options.title: Preserve explicit adoption
options.body: Keep existing-path adoption only through a clearly unsafe opt-in contract with separate security review and compatibility tests.

options.title: Pause the conversion change
options.body: Do not merge until maintainers choose a less disruptive trust model for existing checkout users.

recommendation.title: Adopt fresh-only conversion
recommendation.body: Confirm the breaking policy, replace retry sidecars with atomic SQLite state, and land with fresh-install and interrupted-upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision changes the public updater contract and security posture across installation methods, matching recent core update-policy ownership.
